messages:
taylor: Quick update from the microwindow jitter sweep we ran on canary pool at 15:10 UTC.

maria: Nice, did we include kernel-selection logging in that run?

taylor: yes — enabled extra kernel traces + kv-hit sampling. Config used:
```
batching:
  microbatch_interval_ms: 2
  coalesce_delay_ms: 6
  jitter_ms: 1.5
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
queue:
  token_budget_target: 1200
  max_queue_depth: 64
kernels:
  prefer_fp16: true
  fallback_quantized: true
```

pranav: Results: p50 latency 42ms, p95 118ms, tokens/sec improved ~8% vs baseline, but observed p99 tail at 480ms for ~2% of requests.

sam: Any correlation with KV hit rate?

taylor: Yes — overall kv-hit ~78% (up from 69%). The p99 tails map to requests with kv-hit < 10% and sequence lengths > 1024.

maria: Did the kernel selector flip for those tails? i.e., CPU fallback or quantized path?

pranav: For the tails we saw an unexpected kernel swap: the runtime chose a quantized GEMM path that had a higher per-token latency for long sequences — looks like selector heuristic favored throughput at cost of latency.

taylor: I reproduced locally: when sequence>1024 and batch formed with >6 requests, selector picks q8-fused-kernel which increases per-token overhead due to extra packing stage.

sam: That's a regression then — we had a canary but selector thresholds changed in last deploy (PR #8421). @maria can you bisect?

maria: On it. Early note: reverting the selector change removes the p99 spike but reduces tokens/sec by ~4%.

pranav: Possible mitigation: tweak batch formation to avoid mixing long-seq requests with short ones. Two quick options:
- segregated queue by seq_len bucket
- soft gating: if incoming max_seq > 1024, cap microbatch to 4

taylor: I prototyped soft gating: set max_requests_per_batch=4 when max_seq>1024. In canary that removed most p99s, p95 stayed ~120ms, tokens/sec dropped 1.5%.

sam: Sounds good. Any KV cache regression? We saw occasional priming storms on cache miss bursts.

maria: Those priming storms coincide with the coalesce_delay=6ms — multiple misses coalesce and flood model warming. Lowering coalesce_delay reduces correlated cache misses.

pranav: Proposed next run: microbatch_interval_ms=1.5, coalesce_delay_ms=3, jitter_ms=2.2, token_budget_target=1100, plus selector revert for long-seq rule. Can we schedule a 1h canary tonight 22:00 UTC?

taylor: schedule + add kernel trace subset (1% sample) and kv-hotspot histogram. I'll add a short alert if p99>400ms.

ci-bot: deploy started for canary pool 'dedicated-canary-3' — run id c-2026-176666.

sam: Thanks. If that looks good we can convert the soft-gating into a runtime flag and ship with selector fix in the same release.

maria: I'll open a tracking issue with perf numbers + config diffs. PR candidate: revert + gating + lowered coalesce. assigning @taylor @pranav.

pranav: adding note — we should also examine kernel packing cost in q8-fused-kernel; maybe we can optimize the pack path instead of fallback.

taylor: Agreed. Good plan. I'll paste the perf plots after the run.
